title: Do topic packs make better lessons? (narrow slice, honest simulation)
rules: Briefs and pack topics are fixed here before any run; a change is a new experiment id.
Every run records the sha256 of every prompt it used; a run whose hashes differ from promptHashes is refused unless --unfrozen, and then marked unfrozen.
Every attempt counts: failed and incomplete runs stay in the cost, with status executed/complete/accepted.
Code never judges meaning: overlap is a word n-gram length, evidence is verbatim containment, coverage and correctness are model declarations recorded per checker.
The judge sees shuffled labels and the deck only; the key file is written apart from the scores.

packAdmission.rule: A pack fact is used by the grounded and packed arms only if BOTH checkers answered correct = yes AND neither answered supportedByEvidence = no; a missing verdict fails. Registered before any np1 lesson call; applied in code (pack-arms.ts admitPack) from the verdicts recorded in eval/results/packs/<pack id>/report.json.
